title: These Ants Carry Their Wounded Home and Treat Infected Wounds

scenes.text: These ants rescue their wounded. And they can tell which wounds are infected.
Matabele ants raid termite mounds several times a day. Termite soldiers bite back and take legs.
An injured ant releases a chemical call for help. Nestmates pick it up and carry it home.
Left alone, a third of the injured die. Carried home, almost none do.
If a wound gets infected, nestmates smell it and smear it with germ-killing secretions from a gland.
Untreated, over ninety percent of infected ants die. Treated, around ten. Ants had antibiotics before we did.
scenes.keywords: ant licking wounded ant close up

description:
Matabele ants of sub-Saharan Africa raid termite nests two to four times a day and bring their injured home. An injured ant releases dimethyl disulfide from its mandibular gland as a call for help; carried back, it is usually fighting again by the next raid.
A 2023 Nature Communications study (University of Würzburg) found the ants recognise infected wounds from a change in the ant's surface chemistry and treat them with antimicrobial secretions from the metapleural gland: isolated infected ants died 93 percent of the time, treated ones only about 8 to 22 percent.
Which animal would you trust as a medic?
subject: matabele ant
first_comment: They also triage: an ant missing five of its six legs is left behind, because it could never fight again. Which animal would you trust as a medic?
